questions.q: Which built-in Extended Events session captures deadlock graphs automatically with no setup required?
options: system_health
AlwaysOn_health
telemetry_xevents
default_trace
questions.explain: system_health has captured deadlock graphs in its ring buffer target automatically since SQL Server 2008.

questions.q: What does the resource-list section of a deadlock graph show?
options: The actual locks in conflict — which process owns each resource and which process is waiting for it
A list of every table in the database
The server's total memory usage at the time of the deadlock
The names of every index on the affected tables
questions.explain: resource-list shows the circular wait itself: which process holds a resource the other process needs, and vice versa.

questions.q: By default, how does SQL Server choose which transaction becomes the deadlock victim?
options: It kills whichever transaction is cheapest to roll back
It always kills the transaction that started first
It always kills the transaction with the highest session_id
It asks the DBA to choose in real time
questions.explain: Without DEADLOCK_PRIORITY overrides, SQL Server picks the transaction that costs the least to roll back as the victim.

questions.q: What does SET DEADLOCK_PRIORITY LOW accomplish?
options: It makes that session more likely to be chosen as the deadlock victim
It prevents that session from ever being involved in a deadlock
It raises that session's lock timeout to infinite
It disables deadlock detection for that session entirely
questions.explain: A lower deadlock priority makes a session a more likely victim, useful for letting low-value background jobs absorb retries.

questions.q: Why doesn't a deadlock require a DBA to intervene in real time the way ordinary blocking might?
options: SQL Server detects the circular wait and resolves it automatically within milliseconds by killing a victim
Deadlocks never actually block any queries
Deadlocks only occur in test environments, never in production
SQL Server pauses the entire instance until a DBA manually intervenes
questions.explain: Deadlock detection and resolution is automatic and near-instant; the DBA's work is the after-the-fact root-cause investigation.
